Q: Should long free-text notes be stored/searched in Apache AGE graph nodes or PostgreSQL tables? A:

I agree with you that Elasticsearch would be an overkill for your use case. PostgreSQL's built-in full-text search handles keyword search well, supports ranking, and keeps everything in one database.

I would go with Option 2: store text in PostgreSQL, use AGE only for relationships.

AGE is not built for text search

Apache AGE stores node/edge properties as JSONB internally. It has no full-text search capability, no tsvector, no GIN indexes on text content, no ranking. If you store note bodies on AGE nodes, you'd have to pull all notes into your application and search there, which doesn't scale. I would recommend an arch. like following

PostgreSQL tables          Apache AGE graph
┌──────────────────┐       ┌─────────────────────────────┐
│ notes            │       │ (:Person {id: 1})           │
│  id (PK)         │◄──────│ (:Note {note_id: 42})       │
│  body (TEXT)     │       │ (:Person)-[:HAS_NOTE]->     │
│  body_tsv        │       │          (:Note)            │
│  created_at      │       └─────────────────────────────┘
└──────────────────┘
  • PostgreSQL notes table: Stores the actual text, with a tsvector column for full-text search
  • AGE :Note node: Stores only note_id (foreign key back to the table) — used for graph traversal
  • AGE edges: (:Person)-[:HAS_NOTE]->(:Note), (:Account)-[:MENTIONS]->(:Note), etc.

Setting up full-text search

-- Table
CREATE TABLE notes (
    id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    body TEXT NOT NULL,
    body_tsv TSVECTOR GENERATED ALWAYS AS (to_tsvector('english', body)) STORED,
    created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT now()
);

-- GIN index for fast keyword search
CREATE INDEX idx_notes_fts ON notes USING GIN (body_tsv);

-- Search
SELECT id, ts_headline('english', body, q) AS snippet
FROM notes, to_tsquery('english', 'Bob & green') q
WHERE body_tsv @@ q
ORDER BY ts_rank(body_tsv, q) DESC;

Query pattern: graph traversal + text search

Find all notes connected to a person, filtered by keyword:

-- Step 1: Get note IDs from graph traversal
SELECT * FROM cypher('my_graph', $$
    MATCH (:Person {name: 'Bob Maynard'})-[:HAS_NOTE]->(n:Note)
    RETURN n.note_id
$$) AS (note_id agtype);

-- Step 2: Search within those notes
SELECT id, ts_headline('english', body, q) AS snippet
FROM notes, to_tsquery('english', 'color & green') q
WHERE id IN (/* note_ids from step 1 */)
  AND body_tsv @@ q;

Or combine in a single query using a CTE:

WITH graph_notes AS (
    SELECT (n.note_id::text)::int AS nid
    FROM cypher('my_graph', $$
        MATCH (:Person {name: 'Bob Maynard'})-[:HAS_NOTE]->(n:Note)
        RETURN n.note_id
    $$) AS (note_id agtype), 
    LATERAL (SELECT note_id AS n) sub
)
SELECT id, ts_headline('english', body, q)
FROM notes, to_tsquery('english', 'green') q
WHERE id IN (SELECT nid FROM graph_notes)
  AND body_tsv @@ q;

Q: Why am i getting a error running send2trash A:

For Jupyter Notebook, the program may still be running even if the window is closed.

Looking at the "Home" screen (i.e. not inside any file), if you click on the "Running" tab next to "Files" it will show what kernels are still running under the "KERNELS" section.

If there is one or more that's still active from the folder you're trying to delete, you can shut it down using the icons on the same line as the "KERNELS" section header or by hitting the "x" that appears when you hover over the program.

Shutting these down should let you delete/rename the folder afterwards.

Q: How can I prevent \n showing in text in Mule A:

From the question what i understood is :

  1. You dont want \n to appear in the output, and
  2. Also you want to replace \n with actual linebreak so that your output looks more beautiful.

You can actually do that.Here is how to achieve this with example.

I create a very simple flow and took two payload transformer (see Images).

In first set payload i am just assigning the value

customers who bought this also bought:\n\n- Mario Kart

In the second set payload i am again doing something like

#[payload.replace("\\n", System.getProperty("line.separator"))]

and this produces a formatted result .

Hope this helps ....
